simple.meaning: שָׁקַט (shâqaṭ) is a Hebrew concept word meaning “to repose (usually figurative).” BibleIQ follows how Scripture develops this idea across its occurrences.
simple.biblicalBackground: The concept appears 42 times across Joshua, Judges, Ruth, 2 Kings, 1 Chronicles, and 8 more, beginning at Joshua 11:23. Its contexts include family line, death, land, Israel.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to שָׁקַט (H8252).
simple.whyItMatters: Concept words shape biblical themes. BibleIQ keeps the concept grounded in actual verse evidence instead of starting with a later theological definition.
simple.summary: שָׁקַט (shâqaṭ) / H8252 is traced through Joshua 11:23, Joshua 14:15, Judges 3:11, Judges 3:30 as a generated source-based concept entry.

definitions.usage: appease, idleness, (at, be at, be in, give) quiet(-ness), (be at, be in, give, have, take) rest, settle, be still.
